approach: Extend the existing `check_environment_reach` in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs`. No new `step!` line is added. Add a cache/artifact trigger and six word lists beside the `ENV_*` lists. The trigger fires in two cases. (1) A behavior criterion has a cache or artifact word and a CI word (`ci`, `workflow`, `workflows`, `runner`, `runners`, `github`, `actions`) in the same criterion, read through `scan_segments` so paths and identifiers like `cache.rs` or `cache_dir` do not count. (2) A created or modified `.github/workflows/` deliverable exists and any criterion or the summary has a cache or artifact word. When it fires, one `Environment:` assumption must hold a cache/artifact word, a save word, a restore word, a write-rights word and a scope word. `environment_assumptions` and `plain_words` are reused. The early return and completeness block are restructured so a cache-only trigger demands only the cache statement. The error names each missing part and tells the reader what to write. The doc comment gets a paragraph naming the root cause, the two jobs, the two introspections, and the intended-refusal sentence with 3%. New unit tests go in `reading.rs`; new corpus cases and a declaration test go in `refusal_corpus.rs`; a CHANGELOG item is added. Revision: criterion 6 now sets `fails_without`: the full-workspace run fails on formatting, on any warning, or on the new tests if the check is removed or too broad.

decisions.choice: Extend `check_environment_reach` instead of adding a new check and `step!` line.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says to extend it. The check already makes the reader state site, permissions and data; cache save/restore/write scope is a fourth fact of the same kind. No new function means no change to `refusing_check`, the step-order test `environment_reach_has_one_step_line`, or the acceptance doc list.

rejected.why: It adds a step line, a refusing corpus case requirement and a doc-list entry. It splits one `Environment:` statement across two checks, with two error texts for one missing assumption.

rejected.option: Add the cache words to the existing site/permission/data lists
rejected.why: Those lists only test for the presence of one word each. They cannot tell the reader which of save scope, restore scope or write rights is missing.

decisions.choice: The workflow deliverable raises the cache requirement only when a criterion or the summary has a cache/artifact word. A behavior criterion raises it only when the same criterion also has a CI word.
decisions.reason: Existing tests use workflow deliverables with no cache word and `CI_ENVIRONMENT` (reading.rs around lines 4422, 4464 and 4851, and corpus cases `environment-ci-workflow-*`). Requiring cache scope for every workflow would break them and demand cache facts from a workflow with no cache. Product wording such as 'the reader caches the survey' names no CI place, so it must stay accepted.

rejected.option: Every workflow deliverable needs cache scope
rejected.why: It breaks at least three existing tests and the pages.yml and lint.yml corpus cases, and refuses workflows that have no cache.

rejected.option: Any behavior criterion with the word cache or artifact
rejected.why: It refuses ordinary in-process caches, which are not CI caches.

decisions.choice: Match words through `scan_segments` for behavior criteria, and `plain_words` for the `Environment:` text.
decisions.reason: `scan_segments` ends a run at a path, identifier or non-command backticked span, so `cache.rs` and `cache_dir` do not trigger it. This matches how the existing host-action trigger avoids `pr.rs`. `plain_words` is what the existing completeness test uses for assumption text.

rejected.option: Substring search on the criterion text
rejected.why: It fires on paths and identifiers and on words like 'cached' inside other words.

decisions.choice: The required `Environment:` assumption must hold five lexical parts in one assumption: a cache/artifact noun, a save word, a restore word, a write-rights word and a scope word. The error lists each missing part from the union of all `Environment:` assumptions.
decisions.reason: This follows the accepted reading and the brief's example ('saved by the main branch push run, restored by pull request runs of the same branch and by main, written only by main'). It makes the reader answer the three questions in the root cause: which ref saves, which runs restore, which may write shared entries.

rejected.option: Only a cache/artifact word and a scope word
rejected.why: A sentence that says nothing about who writes shared entries would satisfy it, which is the gap in both jobs.

decisions.choice: Name the new corpus declaration test for the cache scope and keep the check name `check_environment_reach` in the acceptance-check name list.
decisions.reason: No new step exists, so the list already holds the name. The new test asserts it is present, that the doc comment holds the new cause text and ids, that the changelog holds 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', and that `replay_declaration` reads a 3% share. This is what criterion 5 can mean when the check is extended rather than added.

rejected.option: Add a second check name only to satisfy the wording of criterion 5
rejected.why: It would be a new step with no function behind it.

decisions.choice: Criterion 6 is demonstrated by the three Athena checks run together, and its fails_without is stated in terms of what each would catch for this change.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for a behavior criterion to say what fails without the behavior. The full `cargo test --locked` includes the new refusal tests, which fail with the check removed, and the new accept controls, which fail if the trigger is too broad; fmt and clippy fail on unformatted or warning-producing code.

rejected.option: Leave criterion 6 without fails_without as a pure tool-pass criterion
rejected.why: Athena refuses a behavior criterion demonstration with no stated failure.

files.purpose: Add ENV_CACHE_WORDS, ENV_CI_WORDS, ENV_SAVE_WORDS, ENV_RESTORE_WORDS, ENV_WRITE_RIGHTS_WORDS and ENV_SCOPE_WORDS; add the cache trigger, restructure the early return, add the cache-scope completeness test and error; extend the doc comment with the root cause, ids and the 3% sentence.
Add unit tests: refusal and acceptance for a workflow and for a behavior criterion, each missing part named, the class test with both job shapes and unaffected readings, and the doc/changelog test.
Add refuse and accept corpus cases in environment_cases(), new INPUT_FORMS tags with the length updated, and the declaration test with the 3% share.
Add an Unreleased item naming the cause and the cache-scope requirement, with 'expected 3% of newly refused readings'.

steps: In surveys.rs, add the constants after ENV_ABSENT_WORDS: ENV_CACHE_WORDS (cache, caches, cached, caching, artifact, artifacts), ENV_CI_WORDS (ci, workflow, workflows, runner, runners, github, actions), ENV_SAVE_WORDS (save, saves, saved, saving, store, stores, stored, upload, uploads, uploaded), ENV_RESTORE_WORDS (restore, restores, restored, restoring, download, downloads, downloaded, reuse, reuses, reused), ENV_WRITE_RIGHTS_WORDS (write, writes, written, writable, readonly, permission, permissions) and ENV_SCOPE_WORDS (branch, branches, ref, refs, main, default, pr, prs, pull, scope, scoped).

In check_environment_reach, compute cache_trigger: any behavior criterion whose scanned words hold a cache word and a CI word, or a non-delete workflow deliverable with a cache word in any criterion text or the summary (scanned through scan_segments). Add it to the early-return condition and to triggers with a message naming CI caches and stored artifacts. Keep the existing block for workflows, host actions and located reads. When cache_trigger holds, accept if one Environment: assumption (via plain_words) holds a cache word, a save word, a restore word, a write-rights word and a scope word; otherwise push a problem naming each missing part from the union of all Environment: assumptions (the cache or artifact it applies to; which ref and event saves it; which runs restore it; which runs may write shared entries), with a repair sentence quoting the brief's example. Extend the doc comment: the root cause, jobs 20261025-034731-2am0 and 20261025-055626-er96, introspections 20261025-050603-wrv7 and 20261025-065849-n99a, the triggers, and 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended, expected 3% of newly refused readings (an estimate, not measured).'

In reading.rs tests, add environment_reach_cache_refuses_a_workflow_with_a_cache_without_scope, environment_reach_cache_refuses_a_behavior_cache_criterion_without_scope (each part missing in turn, error naming the part; accepted with the brief's sentence), environment_reach_cache_scope_covers_the_class (the 2am0 and er96 shapes plus the unaffected readings) and environment_reach_cache_scope_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause.

In refusal_corpus.rs, add the new tags to INPUT_FORMS and fix its length, add the six cases to environment_cases() with sources naming jobs 20261025-034731-2am0 and 20261025-055626-er96 (rebuilt from the job brief), and add environment_cache_scope_refusal_is_declared_intended (3% share, check name in the list, doc needles, changelog sentence).

In CHANGELOG.md, add an Unreleased Added item at the top: the cause (no step asking, for each CI cache or stored artifact, which ref saves it, which runs restore it, which runs may write shared entries), the extension of check_environment_reach, the requirement of an Environment: assumption stating save scope, restore scope and write rights, the test names, and 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended, expected 3% of newly refused readings.'

Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo test -p athena-core, cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked; fix fixtures or wording until all pass.

risks.risk: False positives: a CI word and a cache word in the same behavior criterion with no CI cache involved (for example 'CI checks that the cache module compiles').
risks.mitigation: The refusal only asks for one extra Environment: assumption and the error says what to write. scan_segments drops paths and identifiers. The 3% share is declared and measured by the replay at verification. Accept-case tests cover the in-process cache and path-only cases.

risks.risk: A reading built for a new test trips an earlier check in refusing_check before check_environment_reach, so refuser names another check.
risks.mitigation: Build fixtures from workflow_reading and behavior_reading, which the existing environment tests already pass through the gate, and assert check_environment_reach directly as well as refuser. Adjust fixture wording, not the check, if an earlier check fires.

risks.risk: The new changelog item or doc text breaks an existing test that finds the item by the old CAUSE string, or that expects only one declared share.
risks.mitigation: Write the new item and doc paragraph with different cause wording, keep the old paragraph and item unchanged, so the first item containing the old CAUSE stays the old one.

risks.risk: The lexical word lists let a sentence meet them without being true, or reject a valid phrasing.
risks.mitigation: State the limit in the doc comment as the existing check does; test the brief's example sentence and the words in each list; word the error to tell the reader what to add.

risks.risk: The records of jobs 2am0 and er96 are not in the snapshot, so corpus wording is rebuilt from their ids and the brief.
risks.mitigation: State 'rebuilt from the job brief' in each case's source, as the existing environment cases do.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in `reading.rs` call `refuser(&reading)` and `check_environment_reach(&reading)` on constructed readings. (a) Fixture: `workflow_reading(Create)` with the path changed to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and a content criterion 'ci.yml saves a result cache keyed by the fingerprint'. With `CI_ENVIRONMENT` only, the check refuses and the error names the missing save, restore and write parts; leaving out one part at a time gives one refusal per part, each naming that part. (b) Fixture: `behavior_reading(&["The CI job restores a result cache keyed by the build fingerprint"])`, refused likewise. (c) Accepted with 'Environment: the CI cache is saved by the main branch push run, restored by pull request runs of the same branch and by main, written only by main' added through `with_environment`; for the workflow `CI_ENVIRONMENT` is also added. A negative control keeps the workflow with no cache word and with `CI_ENVIRONMENT` accepted.
demonstrations.observes: Refused with 'missing' naming the cache save scope, restore scope or write rights for each incomplete assumption; accepted when the assumption states them; the workflow-only control is accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the new trigger and requirement removed, `refuser` returns `None` and `check_environment_reach` returns `Ok`, so every refuse assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points are `check_environment_reach` and `refusing_check` (via the existing `refuser` helper in the reading.rs environment tests). The fixtures are `workflow_reading`, `behavior_reading`, `with_environment` and `CI_ENVIRONMENT`, which exist. The test only builds a `Reading`; no double holds the logic. Step 3 adds the tests.

demonstrations.method: A class test with readings from both jobs. (i) 2am0 shape: ci.yml workflow plus a behavior criterion 'CI restores a result cache keyed by the fingerprint of the build paths'. (ii) er96 shape: an early-push reading with a ci.yml deliverable and a criterion 'the early commit saves the toolchain cache and its CI run is reused at landing'. Each is refused without cache scope and accepted with a complete assumption. (iii) A reading with no cache or artifact word and no workflow, e.g. `behavior_reading(&["Fixed where it originates", "The reader caches the survey in memory"])`, passes `check_environment_reach` unchanged. A second negative control uses a cache word inside a path (`cache.rs is not changed`).
demonstrations.observes: Both job shapes are refused and then accepted, and the unrelated readings stay accepted. The test says the wording is rebuilt from the job ids, since the records are absent from the snapshot.
demonstrations.fails_without: The refusals of (i) and (ii) fail without the new check. If the trigger were made too broad, the (iii) acceptances fail instead.
demonstrations.seam: Same entry points and helpers as criterion 3 (`refuser`, `check_environment_reach`, `behavior_reading`, `workflow_reading`, `with_environment`). They exist. Step 3 adds the test.

The existing tests `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` and the gate/refusing_check agreement test also run.

open_questions: User: Should a cache or artifact word in a behavior criterion with no CI word (for example 'the reader caches the survey') stay accepted? The plan assumes it does, because it names no CI place and the accepted reading ties the rule to CI caches.
